comparisons.peer_topic: Adaptive Computing and Embedded Systems Portfolio Expansion
comparisons.peer_summary: AMD expanded its adaptive computing portfolio with the launch of Versal Series Gen 2 devices, including Versal AI Edge and Prime Series Gen 2 adaptive SoCs, which integrate preprocessing, AI inference, and postprocessing for end-to-end acceleration of AI-driven embedded systems.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and AMD describe the expansion of their hardware portfolios to address the AI PC market, focusing on devices that integrate processing capabilities for AI at the edge. Intel introduced the Core Ultra processor family to serve as the CPU for the AI PC, enabling client-level AI capabilities. Similarly, AMD expanded its adaptive computing portfolio with Versal Series Gen 2 devices, which integrate preprocessing, AI inference, and postprocessing for end-to-end acceleration of AI-driven embedded systems. While Intel focuses on the central processing unit for the broad AI PC market, AMD highlights specific adaptive SoCs for embedded AI applications, reflecting distinct product approaches to the same underlying market trend of on-device AI acceleration.

sentences.text: We recently introduced our Intel Core Ultra processor family that serves as the CPU for the AI PC, which enables AI capabilities at the client level.

We expanded our adaptive computing portfolio with differentiated solutions with the launch of the new Versal™ Series Gen 2 devices, including the new Versal AI Edge Series Gen 2 and Versal Prime Series Gen 2 adaptive SoCs, which bring preprocessing, AI inference, and postprocessing together in a single device for end-to-end acceleration of AI-driven embedded systems.
